paper_verdict.estimator_family: panel fixed effects (OLS within), with robustness checks using FE with AR(1) errors and GLS random effects
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Outcome is log TFP computed as a Cobb-Douglas residual (not output or labour productivity directly); exposure is log of the DESI composite index, so the coefficient is an elasticity to an index, not to a technology stock or usage measure. Sample of 28 units includes the EU aggregate alongside the 27 member states, with only 6 years (2017-2022). Estimates 988-1 to 988-4 and 988-6 to 988-8 are overlapping re-estimations on the same data, not independent. 988-5 uses the TFP index (TFP in 2020 = 1) in levels, so its units differ from the log-TFP estimates. The author states the model 'proves the causal effect' on the strength of FE alone; no IV, lags or other treatment of reverse causality.

paper_verdict.estimator_family: cross-sectional OLS with HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors, split-sample (developing vs developed)
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Single cross-section (2023) with no panel or time dimension; no instruments, lags or other treatment of endogeneity, so estimates are correlations. Outcome is the inverse hyperbolic sine of annual GDP per capita growth (a growth rate, not a productivity level), exposure is the min-max normalized Network Readiness Index (0-1), so coefficients are not elasticities and are not on the scale of log-level specifications. Missing trade data were median-imputed. Developed and developing coefficients have opposite signs and 1192-3 is a re-estimation of 1192-2 on a subsample (Malta and Singapore dropped), so the three estimates are not independent. 'Developing' cohort (N=76) is every non-high-income economy by the 2023 World Bank classification, so it mixes income levels. NRI is a composite ICT readiness index, so its fit as the focal technology depends on how the pooled analysis defines the technology.
